A question arises as to whether a revisional court Patna High Court CR. REV. No.289 of 2025(3)
dt.07-05-2025 can set aside an order of conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court and affirmed by the Court of Appeal, on the basis of such compromise, which has not been accepted as yet by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Rohtas at Sasaram.
8.

sentences.text:
The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioner relies on a judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajendra Bhagat Vs. State of Jharkhand & Anr. (Criminal Appeal No.2 of 2022)
decided on 03.01.2022.
9.

entities.text: Rajendra Bhagat Vs. State of Jharkhand & Anr. (Criminal Appeal No.2 of 2022)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is ascertained from the fact of the above- mentioned decision that the High Court of Jharkhand after taking note of the settlement between the parties, who resolved their marital discord and are leading a happy conjugal life, has confirmed the conviction of the appellant under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, while reducing the sentence to the period of imprisonment already undergone by the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Rajesh Prasad @ Rajesh Seth vs The State Of Bihar on 7 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 10. The Hon'ble Supreme Court taking note of the terms of settlement arrived at by and between the parties, allowed the appeal and I.A. No.6052 of 2020 moved before the High Court in Criminal Revision No.910 of 2019 and all the proceedings arising out of the said FIR No.204 of 2014 are quashed qua the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Rajesh Prasad @ Rajesh Seth vs The State Of Bihar on 7 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, the order of conviction of the appellant is set aside.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the petitioners have not filed such application praying for settlement of the criminal case.

sentences.text: 12. On the other hand, the petitioners are relying upon some terms of settlement arrived at by and between Rajesh Prasad @ Rajesh Seth and Meena Devi at the time of filing of the petition for mutual divorce.
sentences._hearing_file: Rajesh Prasad @ Rajesh Seth vs The State Of Bihar on 7 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The fact of the decision rendered by the Supreme Court is distinguishable with the facts of these cases.
sentences._hearing_file: Rajesh Prasad @ Rajesh Seth vs The State Of Bihar on 7 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 13. For the reasons stated above, this Court is not in a position to admit the instant revision, as the prayers made in both the revisions are misconceived.

sentences.text: 14. The petitioners, however, are at liberty to file appropriate application after settlement of the dispute in the Family Court and passing of decree for mutual divorce for appropriate relief against the order of conviction and sentence passed in Complaint Case No.560 of 2001 and affirmed in Criminal Appeal No.37 of 2016.
sentences._hearing_file: Rajesh Prasad @ Rajesh Seth vs The State Of Bihar on 7 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 15. With the above order, both the revisions are summarily dismissed.
